p.i: Dimensis spatiis sic angulus exeat æquus: Unde fit, ut rectus recte dicatur Horizon. Hic orbis quibus est situs, una nocte diéque Conspiciunt totum se circum volvere cœlum, Et geminus mundi vertex diclinis utrinque Radit Horizontem, geminoque in vertice stellæ Perspicuè surgunt is omni nocte cadúntque Et tarda in ventum demergunt lumina pontum. At vero quando æquantis prope segmina cycli Illinc obtusus, hinc angulus exit acutus, Finitor sese obliquat, Polus alter in undis Condi\ur, Antipodum regnis illustris, at alter Ducit in occidua puppes per cærula flamma, Et dirimit cœlum ac terras obliquus Horizon, Nec totum nobis facit unquam visile cœlum. Hos finitores sed partes semper in æquas Innumera dirimunt scindentes æthera spira, Perque Polos ducta, sic undique ut exeat idem Angulus, at nomen, multis licet, omnibus unum A medio posuêre dies: sermone vocatur Quippe μεσημβρινὸς Graio, sub culmine cœli Linea quæ Phœbi medium discriminat orbem, Perque caput nostrum gelidâ hinc decurrit ad Arctõn, Inde Polum inferni lucentem in culmine mundi, Quum medius rerum minimas Sol efficit umbras. Hanc quoque sub terris volucri cum denique axe Attigit, effusum chaos illætabile noctis Involuit nobis hominúmque beumque labores, Et simul occasu, simul æquis Phœbus ab ortu Exclusis spatiis, media illic luce refulget, Et nostro adversum radiis illuminat orbem. Quum nobis contrà nox intempesta silentes

page.notes: Verse text, set in italic; the lines are run together into one paragraph because no stanza division is printed. Greek words "μεσημβρινὸς" and "Arctõn" are read with doubt. "beumque" is uncertain: the printed form looks like beûmque. "duĉta" is an uncertain reading of a damaged word. The page is clean, with a few light marks in the margins which are not printed text.
